title: SECURITY: oauth2.json with live Yahoo access+refresh tokens is committed to git
description:
oauth2.json is tracked in git (added in commit 399e9b4) and contains a real access_token and refresh_token for the Yahoo Fantasy API, along with consumer key/secret.

.gitignore has a pattern 'oauth2.*.json' which does NOT match the plain filename 'oauth2.json' -- so the ignore rule that was presumably meant to cover this misses it.

Required actions:
 1. Revoke the Yahoo app credentials at https://developer.yahoo.com/apps/ and issue a new consumer key/secret. The tokens in git history must be treated as compromised regardless of what happens to the file.
 2. git rm --cached oauth2.json
 3. Change .gitignore pattern to 'oauth2*.json' so both forms are covered.
 4. Decide whether to scrub git history (git filter-repo / BFG). If the repo is or ever becomes public this is mandatory; if it stays private, revocation alone may be acceptable -- owner's call.
 5. ybot_setup already writes oauth2.json, so nothing needs to change in the normal setup flow.

This is the highest-priority item in the backlog and is independent of all the scoring work.
acceptance_criteria: Credentials revoked; oauth2.json untracked; .gitignore covers oauth2*.json; history decision recorded.

title: ranking_score uses un-shrunk per_game, so 1-game players rank #1 overall
description:
In scoring.score_dataframe():

    df['projected_total'] = df['per_game'] * projected_games
    df['ranking_score']   = df['projected_total']

per_game is the RAW rate, not shrunk_per_game. The comment even says '# projected_total uses per_game (not shrunk) per your request'. This defeats the entire empirical-Bayes shrinkage the module exists to provide.

Verified on data/QuantHockey_2024-2025.xlsx, top 10 by ranking_score:
    Zayne Parekh   D  1 GP  raw 11.2  ranking 918.4   <- #1 overall
    Leon Draisaitl F 71 GP  raw 768   ranking 887.0
    Taylor Ward    F  1 GP  raw 10.4  ranking 852.8   <- #3 overall
    Justin Sourdif F  1 GP  raw  9.2  ranking 754.4   <- #8 overall

Three of the top eight players in the league are 1-game call-ups. shrunk_per_game is computed correctly but then never used for ranking.

Note the multi-file path (score_multiple_files -> combined_ranking_score) DOES aggregate shrunk_per_game, so rank_players.py happens to dodge this because it always prefers combined_*. The bug bites anyone calling score_dataframe directly, or any single-file path, and it makes the per-file ranking_score column in the output actively misleading.

Fix: ranking_score should be shrunk_per_game * projected_games. Keep per_game * projected_games available as a separate column if the raw view is wanted.
acceptance_criteria: score_dataframe ranks a 1-GP player below a comparable 70-GP player. Regression test pins this with the Parekh/Draisaitl case.
notes: OWNER DECISION 2026-09-11: rank on shrunk_per_game. ranking_score = shrunk_per_game * projected_games. Expose the raw per_game projection as a separate column if useful, but shrunk is the default sort.
close_reason: Fixed and regression-tested; see tests/test_scoring_fixes.py and updated tests/test_scoring_characterization.py

title: Goalies score 0 on real QuantHockey data; per_game is a fabricated constant
description:
The goalie support added in 399e9b4 / df03743 / ce7796c produces no real signal on the data it was written for.

Verified against data/QuantHockey_2024-2025.xlsx (1000 rows, 82 goalies):
  * The sheet has 50 columns and NONE of W, GA, SV, SO, SV%, GAA. It is a skaters-and-goalies *skater-stat* export.
  * Goalies are still detected (Pos == 'G'), so score_row() takes the goalie branch -- and every goalie stat resolves to 0.0. goalie raw_score is 0.0 for all 82 goalies.
  * per_game then falls to the 'gp-fallback' path, where goalie_mean has no non-zero goalies to average, so it uses the hardcoded DEFAULT_GOALIE_PER_GAME = 1.98 scaled by +/-20% of GP.
  * Net result: goalie per_game ranges 1.60-2.66 and is a strictly monotonic function of games played. Ranking goalies by this score is identical to sorting them by GP. Top 5 'goalies' are just the 5 highest-GP goalies, all with raw_score 0.0.

So --goalie-method stats|gp-fallback|constant all collapse to the same made-up number on real input.

Options: (a) source actual goalie stats (QuantHockey has a separate goalie export) and read them as a second input, (b) drop goalie scoring and exclude Pos=='G' from the ranking with an explicit warning, (c) keep the fallback but make it loudly WARN that goalie stats were not found. Do not leave it silently fabricating.
acceptance_criteria: Either goalie stats are actually consumed, or the code warns/errors when goalie stat columns are absent instead of emitting a fabricated constant. Test asserts behavior on a goalie-stat-free sheet.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED (2026-09-11): score_dataframe() gained goalie_stats_df /
goalie_name_col / source_name params; score_multiple_files() gained
--goalie-input / --goalie-sheet / --goalie-header (plumbed through
scripts/rank_players.py). When goalie_stats_df is supplied, goalie rows in
the main sheet are matched by Name and rescored for real using
DEFAULT_GOALIE_WEIGHTS (score_row already takes the goalie branch once
W/GA/SV/SO are present); per_game is then raw_score/gp using the MAIN
sheet's GP (goalies are still exempt from shrinkage, see new follow-up
yahoo_fantasy_bot-bq3). New goalie_stats_fabricated bool column marks any
goalie row whose per_game is still the GP-based/constant fabrication
(no --goalie-input match, no same-sheet stats) -- carried through
score_multiple_files as goalie_stats_fabricated_f{idx} and included in
rank_players.py's output CSV. A stderr WARNING now fires (naming the
source file/path and the affected row count) whenever a goalie row falls
back to fabrication, instead of silently fabricating.

Fixture-tested against a hand-built goalie-stats export (no real
QuantHockey goalie export exists yet -- see tests/fixtures/make_goalie_fixture.py
and tests/fixtures/quanthockey_goalie_sample.xlsx): tests/test_scoring_fixes.py::
test_goalie_input_scores_matched_goalies_for_real_fow,
test_goalie_input_unmatched_goalie_still_fabricated_and_warns_fow,
test_no_goalie_input_warns_loudly_with_file_and_count_fow.

NOT DONE (blocked on yahoo_fantasy_bot-nr7): end-to-end validation against
data/ -- there is still no real goalie-stats export to run --goalie-input
against on the actual 2024-25 season. Leaving this issue OPEN until nr7
lands and the path can be validated against real data.

Also filed yahoo_fantasy_bot-bq3: once real goalie stats are wired in,
goalies are still exempt from shrinkage entirely, so a 1-GP goalie can
outrank a full-season goalie (verified against the fixture).

title: ybot --score: scoring subprocess is nested under 'if --no-per-game' and never runs
description:
In scripts/ybot (lines ~116-132), the block that appends --rank-extra, prints the command, and actually runs subprocess.run() is indented INSIDE 'if args.get("--no-per-game"):'.

Consequence: even if the docopt bug (yahoo_fantasy_bot-ulo) is fixed, --score only does anything when --no-per-game is ALSO passed. With --score alone, cmd_parts is built and then silently discarded; no scoring runs, no CSV is written, and the bot proceeds with no scored data and no warning.

Introduced by commit f77493c ('last changes before drafting tomorrow'), which re-indented this block while renaming --scoring-params to --rank-extra. In the prior commit 85f4d35 the block was correctly at the 'if --score' level.

Fix: dedent the block back to the 'if args.get("--score")' level.
acceptance_criteria: ybot --score (without --no-per-game) invokes scripts/rank_players.py; test asserts the subprocess command is built and executed.
close_reason: Fixed: dedented the --rank-extra/print/subprocess.run block back to the 'if args.get("--score")' level so it runs independent of --no-per-game. Covered by tests/test_ybot_cli.py::test_build_score_command_without_no_per_game.

title: ybot --score fails to parse: docopt mis-parses the --goalie-method line
description:
`ybot --score my.cfg` exits with a docopt usage error and never runs.

Root cause: in scripts/ybot the option line

    --goalie-method=<m> Goalies scoring method: stats|gp-fallback|constant. Overrides scoring default when --score is used.

uses a SINGLE space between '<m>' and the description. docopt requires two+ spaces to separate an option from its help text, so it treats the whole line as the option spec, splits on whitespace, and takes the LAST '--' token it sees -- which is the '--score' mentioned in the prose. Result (verified via docopt.parse_defaults):
  * '--goalie-method' is never registered at all
  * '--score' is registered a second time as Option(None,'--score',1,None), i.e. as REQUIRING an argument

So 'ybot --score my.cfg' consumes 'my.cfg' as the value of --score, leaving no <cfg_file>, and docopt raises SystemExit.

Repro: ./env/bin/python -c "import docopt; doc=open('scripts/ybot').read().split(chr(34)*3)[1]; docopt.docopt(doc, argv=['--score','x.cfg'])"

Fix: put two spaces before every option description in the Options block, and do not mention other flags by name inside an option description on a line docopt may mis-split.
acceptance_criteria: ybot --score my.cfg parses successfully; --goalie-method appears in docopt.parse_defaults() output; a test asserts both.
close_reason: Fixed: rewrote Options block with consistent 2+ space separation before every description and consistent indentation; --goalie-method now registers correctly (argcount=1) and --score registers exactly once (argcount=0). Verified via docopt.parse_defaults() and end-to-end docopt.docopt(['--score','my.cfg']). Covered by tests/test_ybot_cli.py.

title: Obtain QuantHockey goalie-stats export for data/
description:
Blocks real goalie scoring (yahoo_fantasy_bot-fow). The current data/QuantHockey_*.xlsx files are the skater-stats export -- 50 columns, none of W/GA/SV/SO. QuantHockey publishes a separate goalie-stats page.

ACTION FOR OWNER: download the QuantHockey goalie stats export for 2024-2025 (and 2023-2024 for the decay weighting) and drop them in data/ using a distinguishable name, e.g. data/QuantHockey_G_2024-2025.xlsx.

Until this lands, --goalie-input can be implemented and fixture-tested but cannot be validated end to end against real data.
acceptance_criteria: data/ contains a goalie-stats export whose columns include W, GA, SV, SO; rank_players --goalie-input scores goalies from real numbers.

title: EPIC: no test coverage for the last 12 commits' functionality
description:
The scoring/draft/CLI work added in commits 2684f21..f77493c ships with three test functions total, and two of the three currently FAIL on a clean checkout.

What exists:
  yahoo_fantasy_bot/tests/test_scoring.py       - score_dataframe on synthetic skaters (passes)
  yahoo_fantasy_bot/tests/test_scoring_more.py  - shrinkage k effect + normalize_file_weights smoke (passes)
  tests/test_runner_cli.py                      - rank_players --help and a smoke run (BOTH FAIL)

What has ZERO coverage:
  * scripts/ybot argument parsing -- would have caught yahoo_fantasy_bot-ulo immediately
  * ybot --score command construction -- would have caught the indentation bug (yahoo_fantasy_bot-gor)
  * ybot -> cfg['Scoring'] wiring -- would have caught the NoSectionError (yahoo_fantasy_bot-glo)
  * goalie scoring on a sheet with no goalie stat columns, i.e. the actual data (yahoo_fantasy_bot-fow)
  * the goalie_method='stats'/'gp-fallback'/'constant' branches
  * shrinkage actually affecting rank order (yahoo_fantasy_bot-t0p)
  * league_mean computation with goalies present (yahoo_fantasy_bot-chg)
  * column alias resolution against the REAL QuantHockey column set (yahoo_fantasy_bot-zop)
  * score_multiple_files decay weighting math, file ordering, empty-input handling
  * rank_players output column selection (yahoo_fantasy_bot-gl7)
  * bot.py scored-CSV merge (yahoo_fantasy_bot-phy)
  * lineup_optimizer ranking-metric branch (yahoo_fantasy_bot-45e)
  * scripts/draft_watcher.py and utils.PlayerDetailsCache -- entirely untested
  * scripts/mock_draft_test.py -- entirely untested

Note the existing tests all use synthetic frames whose column names (PlusMinus, ShotAttempts) do NOT match the real export (+/-, SHOTS). That is precisely why the BLK/BS alias bug survived. New tests must use a fixture built from the real column set.

Approach: build a small committed fixture reproducing the real 50-column QuantHockey schema (a dozen rows incl. goalies), and write characterization tests first so the current behavior is pinned before any refactor.
acceptance_criteria: pytest passes from a clean checkout; every bug in this backlog has a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after.
notes:
Added characterization tests pinning current scoring.py behavior against
the real-schema fixture (tests/fixtures/quanthockey_sample.xlsx via the
new quanthockey_sample_df/quanthockey_sample_path conftest fixtures):
tests/test_scoring_characterization.py covers raw_score on real column
names, the BLK/BS alias bug (yahoo_fantasy_bot-zop), goalies scoring 0
and fabricated per_game across all three goalie_methods
(yahoo_fantasy_bot-fow), league_mean_per_game contamination by goalies
(yahoo_fantasy_bot-chg), ranking_score using unshrunk per_game
(yahoo_fantasy_bot-t0p), the compute_per_game=False path, and

Also added tests/test_utils.py for utils.PlayerDetailsCache (previously

Still uncovered from this epic's list (left for whoever owns those

title: EPIC: the CLI surface is incoherent across four entry points
description:
There are four user-facing entry points with no shared convention:

  scripts/ybot            docopt, installed on PATH via setup.py scripts=
  scripts/ybot_setup      installed on PATH
  scripts/rank_players.py argparse, NOT installed, must be run by relative path from repo root
  scripts/draft_watcher.py argparse, NOT installed, must be run by relative path
  scripts/mock_draft_test.py argparse, NOT installed, undocumented in both READMEs

Concrete problems:
  * Two different arg-parsing libraries with different --help formats and different error behavior.
  * ybot duplicates 18 of rank_players' flags in its own docstring, forwards 5 (yahoo_fantasy_bot-he4), and mis-parses one badly enough to break the whole tool (yahoo_fantasy_bot-ulo).
  * rank_players.py hardcodes Path('data') and writes ranked_players.csv / yahoo_comparison.csv into the CURRENT directory, so it only behaves as documented when cwd is the repo root.
  * ybot shells out to 'python scripts/rank_players.py' via subprocess with a relative path -- it breaks if ybot is run from anywhere but the repo root, even though ybot itself is installed on PATH. It should import the scoring module directly.
  * Nothing tells the user which tool to reach for. ybot manages a roster, rank_players ranks a draft pool, draft_watcher tails a live draft, mock_draft_test simulates one -- but that is only discoverable by reading source.

Proposed direction (needs owner sign-off):
  1. ybot keeps roster management. Replace its 18 scoring flags with a single '--score' plus '--rank-extra="..."' passthrough, OR forward everything -- pick one.
  2. Call the scoring code in-process (from yahoo_fantasy_bot import scoring) instead of subprocess-ing a relative script path.
  3. Install rank_players and draft_watcher as real console_scripts (ybot-rank, ybot-draft-watch) so they work from any cwd.
  4. Standardize on argparse everywhere, or on docopt everywhere.
  5. Add a --data-dir and a --out-dir to rank_players so nothing depends on cwd.

This is the umbrella for the 'CLI isn't clear at all' complaint. Individual defects are tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: One documented way to invoke each tool, working from any cwd, with a consistent --help; README shows exactly those invocations.

title: File ordering for decay weighting is non-reproducible: mtime default breaks on a fresh clone
description:
score_multiple_files applies decay^idx weighting where index 0 must be the NEWEST season. rank_players.py decides that order by file mtime by default.

Git does not preserve mtimes. On a fresh clone every file in data/ gets the checkout timestamp -- verified, both data/*.xlsx currently have identical mtime 1789163757. Ordering then falls back to whatever order sorted() leaves equal keys in, i.e. glob order. So on one machine the 2024-2025 season may be weighted 1.0 and on another 0.5, silently, with no error.

Separately, --reverse is a NO-OP under the default --sort-by mtime. The code does:

    paths = sorted(paths, key=mtime)          # oldest first
    if args.reverse:   paths = reversed(paths)   # -> newest first
    else:
        if sort_by == 'mtime': paths = reversed(paths)   # -> ALSO newest first

Both branches produce the same list. Verified: 'rank_players.py --sort-by mtime' and '--sort-by mtime --reverse' print identical file lists.

Fix: derive season order from the filename (the files are already named QuantHockey_<season>.xlsx), make that the default, and reserve mtime as an explicit opt-in. Always print the resolved order with its assigned weight so the user can see what was used. Fix or remove --reverse.
acceptance_criteria: Ordering is deterministic from a fresh clone; --reverse demonstrably changes the order or is removed; the resolved order and per-file weights are printed.
close_reason: Added season-based default sort (reproducible across clones), fixed --reverse no-op, print resolved order+decay weights; tests/test_rank_players_cli.py

title: pytest is misconfigured: setup.cfg points at a package that does not exist
description:
setup.cfg has:

    [tool:pytest]
    python_files = yahoo_baseball_assistant/tests/*.py

'yahoo_baseball_assistant' is a former name of this project and no such directory exists. python_files is also the wrong option for this -- it is a filename glob for test discovery, not a path restriction, so it silently breaks normal test_*.py discovery.

Compounding problems:
  * Tests live in TWO places with no stated rule: tests/ (test_runner_cli.py, added by the vibe-coded commits) and yahoo_fantasy_bot/tests/ (test_roster.py, test_scoring.py, test_scoring_more.py).
  * tests/test_runner_cli.py shells out with sys.executable and a relative 'scripts/rank_players.py' path, so it only passes if pytest is run from the repo root AND the package is pip-installed. Both currently fail on a clean checkout: 2 failed, 3 passed.
  * .travis.yml's script step is literally: echo "no tests". CI has never run the suite.
  * setup.py declares setup_requires=['pytest-runner'], a deprecated pattern.

Fix: consolidate on one tests/ directory, replace the python_files line with a correct testpaths setting, make the CLI tests locate the script relative to __file__, and give CI a real 'pytest' invocation.
acceptance_criteria: pytest from a clean checkout collects and passes all tests; CI runs pytest rather than echoing; single tests/ location.
close_reason:
Fixed setup.cfg (testpaths=tests replacing the wrong python_files glob
pointed at yahoo_baseball_assistant). Consolidated tests into a single
tests/ dir (git mv test_roster.py, test_scoring.py, test_scoring_more.py,
conftest.py from yahoo_fantasy_bot/tests/, merged conftest content).
Fixed tests/test_runner_cli.py to locate scripts/rank_players.py via a
path derived from __file__ instead of a repo-root-relative string, so it
passes regardless of pytest's invocation cwd. Also fixed a stale
empty_roster fixture (roster.Container() was missing the now-required
cfg arg; added a minimal fake ScoreAccumulator stub so the test doesn't
need the nhl_scraper dependency). Updated .travis.yml to actually run
pytest instead of `echo "no tests"`.

./env/bin/python -m pytest from repo root: 47 passed, 0 failed.

title: README.rst is corrupted: whole document duplicated inside an indented markdown fence
description:
Commit ce7796c ('CLI: add goalie-method and file-order flags; docs: README update') mangled README.rst. Current structure:

  * Lines 1-13: the original header, intro, 'Build status' section, and the travis '.. image::' directive -- but the directive's ':target:' line is GONE.
  * Line 14 onward: a literal '    ```restructuredtext' markdown code fence, 4-space indented, followed by the ENTIRE document again (header, intro, build status, installation, execution, example, plus the new scoring sections), and a closing '    ```' at EOF.

Two consequences:
  * In RST, the 4-space indented block following the .. image:: directive is parsed as directive content / a literal block. Everything after line 13 renders as a code block, not as documentation. GitHub and PyPI both show it broken.
  * setup.py passes README.rst as long_description, so any PyPI upload publishes the broken text.

Fix: rebuild README.rst as a single un-indented RST document -- restore the travis ':target:' line, drop the markdown fence and the duplicated copy, and keep exactly one copy of each section. This should be done together with the doc-accuracy fixes tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: README.rst contains no markdown code fence, no duplicated sections, restores the :target: line, and renders cleanly (docutils rst2html emits no errors).

title: rank_players.py output CSV is Name plus three identical score columns; Team/Pos/GP all dropped
description:
Running scripts/rank_players.py on the real data produces a CSV with exactly these columns:

    Name, combined_shrunk_per_game, combined_projected_total, combined_ranking_score

(and the last two are numerically identical, since combined_ranking_score = combined_projected_total.)

Cause: score_multiple_files() keeps only [Name, gp, shrunk_per_game, projected_total, raw_score] per file and then renames them with a _f0/_f1 suffix. So by the time rank_players builds its column list:
  * default_cols looks for 'Team' -- dropped by score_multiple_files, never present
  * computed looks for bare 'raw_score','gp','per_game','shrunk_per_game','projected_total','adjusted_total','ranking_score' -- all suffixed now, none match
Only the three combined_* columns survive.

Downstream fallout, all currently dead code:
  * The printed top-N table advertises Name/Team/GP/raw_score but can only ever show Name and the score.
  * The 'Handle missing Team column' guard added in 5662978 is permanently taking the missing branch.
  * scripts/mock_draft_test.py reads p.get('Team') for team_abbr -> always None.
  * The committed top100_ranked_players_with_pos.csv cannot be reproduced by any current code path.

Fix: carry Name/Team/Pos (and at least gp from the newest file) through score_multiple_files into the merged frame, and have rank_players select suffixed per-file columns explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: rank_players.py output contains Name, Team, Pos, GP and per-file score columns; smoke test asserts the column set.
close_reason: Fixed and regression-tested; see tests/test_scoring_fixes.py and updated tests/test_scoring_characterization.py

title: BLK weight is never applied: QuantHockey column is 'BS', not in the alias list
description:
scoring.DEFAULT_WEIGHTS includes 'BLK': 1.0 and the module docstring advertises 'Block: +1 each'. But:

    _COLUMN_ALIASES['BLK'] = ('BLK', 'Blocks', 'blocks')

The QuantHockey export uses 'BS' (blocked shots). Verified: 'BLK' in df.columns is False, 'BS' in df.columns is True. So _first_available_value returns 0.0 for every player and the blocks term contributes nothing to any real score.

'HITS' is present in the export too and is not scored at all (no weight, no alias), though that may be intentional.

Fix: add 'BS' (and 'BkS', 'BLKS') to the BLK alias tuple. Decide explicitly whether HITS should be scored and either add it or note in the docstring that it is deliberately excluded.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring a real QuantHockey row produces a non-zero blocks contribution; test asserts BS is picked up by the BLK alias.
close_reason: Fixed and regression-tested; see tests/test_scoring_fixes.py and updated tests/test_scoring_characterization.py

title: league_mean_per_game is contaminated by goalies' zero per_game, biasing all skater shrinkage
description:
In scoring.score_dataframe(), league_mean is computed as

    league_mean = df.loc[df['gp'] > 0, 'per_game'].mean()

This runs BEFORE the goalie fallback assigns goalies a non-zero per_game. At that point all 82 goalies have per_game == 0.0 but gp > 0, so they are included in the mean as zeros.

Verified on data/QuantHockey_2024-2025.xlsx:
    league_mean_per_game (as computed) = 2.0204
    skater-only mean                   = 2.2008
An 8.2% downward bias.

league_mean is the shrinkage target for every skater, and it is also what players with gp == 0 get assigned as their shrunk_per_game outright. So every skater's shrunk rate is pulled toward a value that is too low, and the error scales with the goalie fraction of the sheet.

Fix: compute league_mean over skaters only (~df['is_goalie'] & gp > 0), or compute it after goalie per_game is finalized -- but skater-only is the correct statistic since goalies are exempt from shrinkage anyway.
acceptance_criteria: league_mean_per_game equals the skater-only mean; test with a mixed skater/goalie frame asserts goalies do not move the value.
close_reason: Fixed and regression-tested; see tests/test_scoring_fixes.py and updated tests/test_scoring_characterization.py

title: ybot documents 13 scoring flags that are never forwarded to rank_players.py
description:
scripts/ybot's Options block (and README.rst) advertise these flags as controlling scoring:

  --input --sheet --projected-games --k --weight-by-games --no-weight-by-games
  --normalize-file-weights --yahoo-points-field --fuzzy-match --fetch-yahoo
  --league-id --oauth-file --rank-extra

Only five are actually mapped into cmd_parts: --goalie-method, --sort-by, --reverse, --decay, --no-per-game. The other thirteen are parsed by docopt and then silently dropped -- passing them changes nothing and produces no error or warning.

README.rst's 'Exposed scoring-related options on ybot' section lists all of them as working, so the docs actively lie.

Decision needed: either forward all of them, or cut ybot down to --score plus --rank-extra passthrough and delete the rest from both the CLI and the README. Recommend the latter -- ybot should not be a second copy of rank_players' argument parser.
acceptance_criteria: Every flag ybot advertises either reaches rank_players.py or is removed from the docstring and README. Test asserts the built command line for a representative flag set.
notes: OWNER DECISION 2026-09-11: forward ALL 18 flags from ybot to rank_players.py. Accepted tradeoff: the flag list is duplicated in two files and must be kept in sync by hand. Mitigate with a test that asserts every ybot scoring flag is accepted by rank_players' parser, so drift fails CI.
close_reason: Forward all 18 scoring flags in build_score_command(); added --goalie-input/--goalie-sheet/--goalie-header to ybot; anti-drift test in tests/test_cli_contract.py

title: ybot: cfg.get('Scoring', {}) raises NoSectionError on RawConfigParser
description:
scripts/ybot line 127:

    cfg['Scoring'] = cfg.get('Scoring', {})

cfg is a configparser.RawConfigParser. Its .get() signature is get(section, option, *, fallback=...), NOT dict.get. So this call is interpreted as 'read option {} from section Scoring' and raises configparser.NoSectionError: No section: 'Scoring'.

Verified: RawConfigParser().get('Scoring', {}) -> NoSectionError.

This is the line that is supposed to hand the scored CSV path to the bot, so the --score -> Scoring.scored_csv -> bot.py wiring is broken end to end (third independent defect in the same feature, after yahoo_fantasy_bot-ulo and the indentation bug).

Fix: use
    if not cfg.has_section('Scoring'): cfg.add_section('Scoring')
    cfg['Scoring']['scored_csv'] = out_path
acceptance_criteria: Running ybot --score sets cfg['Scoring']['scored_csv'] without raising; unit test covers it.
close_reason: Fixed: replaced 'cfg["Scoring"] = cfg.get("Scoring", {})' with 'if not cfg.has_section("Scoring"): cfg.add_section("Scoring")' followed by cfg['Scoring']['scored_csv'] = out_path.

title: rank_players.py --input default points at a file that no longer exists
description:
scripts/rank_players.py:

    p.add_argument('--input', default='data/QuantHockey_1759620509.xlsx')

That file was renamed to data/QuantHockey_2024-2025.xlsx in commit df03743. The default now names a nonexistent path.

It 'works' only by accident: the code does 'if args.input and Path(args.input).exists()' and, on the miss, silently falls through to globbing data/*.xlsx. So the documented default behavior and the actual behavior are unrelated, and a user who passes a real --input path with a typo gets the glob too -- silently scoring the wrong files instead of erroring.

The module docstring also still says it reads 'data/QuantHockey_1759620509.xlsx'.

Fix: make --input default to None, glob data/ when it is None, and hard-error when an explicitly-passed --input does not exist. Update the docstring.
acceptance_criteria: --input with a bad path errors instead of silently globbing; default is None; docstring matches behavior.
close_reason: --input now defaults to None, hard-errors on nonexistent explicit path instead of silently globbing; docstring fixed; tests/test_rank_players_cli.py

title: README documents flags that do not exist (--data-dir) and paths that are wrong
description:
Inaccuracies in README.rst's scoring sections, verified against the code:

  * '--data-dir data/' is shown in the primary rank_players example. There is no --data-dir argument; argparse will reject it. The data directory is hardcoded to Path('data').
  * The ybot scoring example invokes './env/bin/python scripts/ybot ...' while the Installation section installs the package, which puts 'ybot' on PATH. Two different invocation styles are shown for the same tool.
  * README_DRAFT_WATCHER.md likewise uses './env/bin/python' throughout and hardcodes a personal league id (nhl.l.2354566) as the example.
  * The '--fetch-yahoo' description says it requires 'my.cfg / oauth2.json'; it actually requires --league-id plus --oauth-file and never reads my.cfg.
  * The goalie-method descriptions describe behavior that does not occur on the real data (see yahoo_fantasy_bot-fow).
  * The ybot flag list documents 13 flags that are not forwarded (see yahoo_fantasy_bot-he4).

Fix as part of the README rewrite tracked in yahoo_fantasy_bot-2ps.
acceptance_criteria: Every command shown in the READMEs runs successfully as written against the repo's own data/ directory.

title: lineup_optimizer silently changes its ranking metric when a scored CSV is present
description:
lineup_optimizer.GeneticAlgorithm (line ~205, added in 85f4d35) changed the 'pct_own' seed generation:

    if 'combined_projected_total' in self.ppool.columns:
        selector.rank(['combined_projected_total'])
    else:
        selector.rank(['percent_owned'])

Issues:
  * The branch is named 'pct_own' but no longer ranks by percent owned. The gen_type name, the log message, and the behavior now disagree.
  * The switch is implicit -- driven by whether a column happens to exist -- with no config flag and no log line saying which metric was used. Two runs with the same config can seed completely differently depending on whether a stale scored_players.csv is lying around.
  * Because of the bot.py fillna(0.0) issue (yahoo_fantasy_bot-*), every player who failed the name merge gets combined_projected_total = 0.0 and is ranked last, which is worse than the percent_owned behavior it replaced.

Fix: make the metric an explicit config option under [LineupOptimizer], log which metric was selected, and rename the gen_type if it is no longer percent-owned based.
acceptance_criteria: Ranking metric is config-driven and logged; test asserts both branches are selectable explicitly.

title: No sample_config.ini exists despite being referenced by ybot and the README
description:
scripts/ybot's usage text says:

    <cfg_file>  The name of the configuration file.  See sample_config.ini for the format.

There is no sample_config.ini anywhere in the repo. MANIFEST.in includes 'yahoo_fantasy_bot/templates/*.ini' -- that directory does not exist either.

The config format is only discoverable by reading source: bot.py and ybot between them require sections [Connection] (oauthFile), [League] (id), [Logger] (file, level), [Scorer] (stdevCap), [LineupOptimizer] (generations, mutationPct), [Cache] (dir), plus whatever ybot_setup writes.

This is a significant part of why the CLI is hard to use -- there is no way to know what a valid config looks like without reverse-engineering it.

Fix: generate a documented sample_config.ini from what ybot_setup actually emits, commit it, and reference it from the README. Optionally have ybot validate required sections up front with a clear error instead of a KeyError deep in the run.
acceptance_criteria: sample_config.ini exists, is referenced by README and ybot, and a test asserts ybot accepts it.

title: bot.py scored-CSV merge swallows all errors and cannot match on the column it needs
description:
bot.py ManagerBot.fetch_player_pool() (added in 85f4d35) wraps its entire scored-CSV merge in:

    try:
        ...
    except Exception:
        pass

Any failure -- missing file, unreadable CSV, missing join column, merge shape error -- is silently discarded and the bot proceeds as if scoring never happened. Given that the --score path is broken three different ways (yahoo_fantasy_bot-ulo, -gor, -glo), this bare except is exactly why none of those failures were ever noticed.

Second problem: it merges left_on='name' (the Yahoo player pool column) against right_on='Name' (the scored CSV column). Yahoo names and QuantHockey names differ in punctuation and accents ('Mitch Marner' vs 'Mitchell Marner', 'Tim Stutzle' vs 'Tim Stuetzle'). An exact string merge will miss a large fraction of players, and the code then does .fillna(0.0), so every miss becomes a score of ZERO rather than 'unknown'. A missed star player is scored as the worst possible option.

Fix: log at warning level instead of pass; catch specific exceptions; report how many pool players matched vs. missed; and leave unmatched players as NaN so downstream code can distinguish 'no data' from 'bad player'. rank_players already has a rapidfuzz path -- reuse that normalization here.
acceptance_criteria: Merge failures are logged with counts; unmatched players are NaN not 0.0; test covers a partial-match case.

title: Dependency metadata is incomplete and inconsistent
description:
The scoring/ranking code added in the last 12 commits imports pandas, numpy, openpyxl (via pd.read_excel on .xlsx) and optionally rapidfuzz. None of these are declared.

  * requirements.txt: no pandas, no numpy, no openpyxl, no rapidfuzz. Pins yahoo_fantasy_api==2.0.1 exactly.
  * setup.py install_requires: no pandas, no numpy, no openpyxl, no rapidfuzz. Asks for yahoo_fantasy_api>=2.4.1 -- which CONTRADICTS the ==2.0.1 pin in requirements.txt.
  * setup.py classifiers claim 'Programming Language :: Python :: 3.5'; the code uses f-strings throughout (3.6+) and pathlib idioms, and .travis.yml targets 3.7.

A fresh 'pip install -r requirements.txt && pip install -e .' cannot run scripts/rank_players.py.

Fix: add pandas, numpy, openpyxl to install_requires; add rapidfuzz as an extras_require['fuzzy']; reconcile the yahoo_fantasy_api version between the two files; correct python_requires and the classifier.
acceptance_criteria: A clean venv following the README install steps can run scripts/rank_players.py against data/ without additional pip installs.
close_reason: Added pandas/numpy/openpyxl to install_requires+requirements.txt, rapidfuzz as extras_require[fuzzy], reconciled yahoo_fantasy_api version, fixed python_requires/classifier; tests/test_dependency_metadata.py

title: Goalies are never shrunk toward a league mean, so a hot 1-GP goalie can outrank full-season goalies once real stats are wired in
description:
Verified via tests/fixtures/quanthockey_goalie_sample.xlsx + --goalie-input:
running scripts/rank_players.py --input tests/fixtures/quanthockey_sample.xlsx
--goalie-input tests/fixtures/quanthockey_goalie_sample.xlsx puts Kaapo
Kahkonen (1 GP, raw_score 14.0) at #2 overall (combined_ranking_score
~1148), ahead of Andrei Vasilevski (63 GP, raw_score 760.0, ~989) and
Samuel Montembeault (62 GP, raw_score 610.0, ~807).

Cause: scoring.py's _shrink() explicitly exempts goalies from empirical-Bayes
shrinkage ("Goalies are exempt from shrink -- use raw per_game"), so
shrunk_per_game == per_game for every goalie regardless of sample size. This
is the same class of problem yahoo_fantasy_bot-t0p fixed for skaters (ranking
on raw per_game let small samples dominate) -- but for goalies it was never
addressed, because until yahoo_fantasy_bot-fow's --goalie-input work, all
goalies had raw_score 0.0 and the issue was invisible.

This couldn't be verified against real data yet since there is no real
QuantHockey goalie export in data/ (blocked on yahoo_fantasy_bot-nr7); it's
confirmed against the hand-built fixture.

Suggested fix: compute a goalie-specific league_mean_per_game (over goalies
only) and apply the same shrinkage formula to goalies using their own GP,
instead of exempting them entirely.

title: score_multiple_files([]) raises bare AttributeError instead of a clear error
description:
scoring.score_multiple_files(file_paths=[]) never assigns `merged` (the
per-file frames list is empty, so the `for f in frames: ...` merge loop
never runs), then unconditionally does `for col in merged.columns:` on
merged=None. This raises:

    AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'columns'

with no indication of what actually went wrong (empty input). Callers
(e.g. scripts/rank_players.py, if it were ever invoked with no discovered
files) get a confusing traceback instead of a clear "no input files"
error.

Pinned today's behavior in tests/test_scoring_characterization.py::test_score_multiple_files_empty_list_raises.

Suggested fix: raise a clear ValueError("score_multiple_files: no file_paths given") early, or return an empty DataFrame with the expected columns.
close_reason: Fixed and regression-tested; see tests/test_scoring_fixes.py and updated tests/test_scoring_characterization.py

title: Generated CSV artifacts and personal draft data are committed at repo root
description:
These are program OUTPUT, checked into git at the repo root by the vibe-coded commits:

  top100_ranked_players.csv, top100_ranked_players_with_pos.csv, top50_ranked_players.csv,
  mock_draft_results.csv, fetched_mock_draft_458.l.177636.csv, fetched_mock_draft_nhl.l.2354566.csv

Problems: they are stale (produced by intermediate versions of the scoring code -- top100_ranked_players_with_pos.csv has a Pos column that no current code path can emit, see yahoo_fantasy_bot-gl7), they embed real league ids, and .gitignore already ignores 'ranked_players.csv' which shows the intent was to keep outputs untracked.

Fix: git rm --cached them, add an out/ or reports/ directory to .gitignore, and default the scripts to writing there. If any are wanted as reference fixtures, move them under tests/fixtures/ with a note on how they were generated.
acceptance_criteria: Repo root has no generated CSVs; .gitignore covers the output directory; scripts default to writing there.

title: Dead goalie_mask code in score_multiple_files can never fire
description:
score_multiple_files() contains ~25 lines of commentary plus this logic:

    pos_col_candidates = [c for c in merged.columns if c.lower()=='position' or c.lower().endswith('.position')]
    if pos_col_candidates: ... build goalie_mask ...

merged is assembled exclusively from cols_to_keep = [key_name, 'gp', 'shrunk_per_game', 'projected_total', 'raw_score'] (plus optional yahoo_score), all suffixed. A column named 'position' can never be present, so pos_col_candidates is always empty, goalie_mask is always all-False, and the 'do not multiply goalies by GP' rule never applies.

The surrounding comment block openly narrates the author trying and abandoning three different heuristics.

Once yahoo_fantasy_bot-* (carry Pos through the merge) is fixed this can be made real; until then it is misleading. Either wire it to the real Pos column or delete it.
acceptance_criteria: Either goalie_mask is driven by a Pos column that actually exists in merged, or the block is removed. Test covers whichever path is chosen.
close_reason: Fixed and regression-tested; see tests/test_scoring_fixes.py and updated tests/test_scoring_characterization.py
